hypothesis: HT-Breakout may have a repeatable route-side interaction: its HYPE long implementation may retain positive after-cost expectancy while the current short implementation and direct transfer to BTC, ETH, or SOL may require different context or exit treatment.
decision: Keep bidirectional v25 execution unchanged and continue the predeclared route-and-side forward challenger. Three post-baseline core-asset longs resolved after actual venue costs: SOL +$1.582877, ETH +$0.011230, and BTC -$0.003446, for +$1.590661 combined. This is encouraging transfer evidence, but the SOL lifecycle supplied 99.30% of gross profit and no new HYPE long or any new HT-Breakout short resolved in the prospective window. Do not add a long-only route, a five-minute alignment gate, a size change, or an exit change from this concentration. Resolve the currently open HT-Breakout lifecycles and compare independent route-side windows before proposing an executable successor.
falsifier: The cross-asset long hypothesis weakens if new independently resolved BTC, ETH, or SOL longs make the forward cohort nonpositive after fees, funding, and slippage, or if performance remains dependent on one SOL winner. The short-side concern weakens if new shorts become positive after costs with stable fill and protection evidence. Missing route-side attribution, changed evidence bytes, a profile mismatch accepted as comparable, or any execution authority in this record invalidates the comparison.
limitations: The prospective cohort contains only three resolved trades and one SOL winner supplied 99.30% of its gross profit.
The BTC and ETH outcomes were economically tiny; their signs could change under modestly different fills or costs.
No new prospective HYPE long or HT-Breakout short resolved, so the original side asymmetry remains untested in a new independent window.
The all-live 21-trade aggregate combines the frozen baseline and three new lifecycles across different times, assets, notionals, and profile generations.
Open lifecycles and marked PnL are excluded; they can materially change the next revision after resolution.
The profit factor is numerically large because the only loss was $0.003446 and must not be interpreted as a stable expected profit factor.
This revision cannot gate, rank, route, size, enter, close, pause, or promote a strategy.
